summary: The main risks are not the Helix data mapping itself, but incomplete backend seams, leaky existing contracts, and projection consistency. Several accepted assumptions conflict with current code paths that still special-case ArangoDB, expose raw SQLite connections, or rely on arbitrary AQL templates.

suggestions.title: Centralize backend opening behind a capability-aware resolver
suggestions.rationale: The wiki factory has an extension registry, but CLI, toolkit, sync, federation, and SourceCollectionManager each special-case ArangoDB and reject or bypass other server backends. `WikiProjectConfig.is_built()` also treats any non-SQLite/non-Arango backend as a local `pages/` directory, so a Helix server configuration can fail before the store opens.

suggestions.title: Replace the ledger connection leak with a repository transaction protocol
suggestions.rationale: Changing `ledger_transaction()` to yield an accumulator is insufficient: `LedgerIndex` still types the value as `aiosqlite.Connection`, issues SQL directly for reads, deletes, cursor state, and rebuilds, while `LedgerService` directly queries `store._read()`. A Helix implementation needs backend-neutral read/reduce/write operations or an explicit event-log projection interface.

suggestions.title: Constrain ontology traversal before removing raw AQL
suggestions.rationale: `TraversalPattern.query_template` and `ResolvedIntent.aql` are arbitrary AQL strings with dynamic parameters and collection binds. `mixin.py`, `entity_resolver.py`, and `authorization.py` execute those templates, including management-chain and `DOCUMENT()` lookups. A few named traversal methods cannot preserve this contract; introduce a validated traversal AST/compiler shared by Arango and Helix, or retain a clearly scoped raw-query capability for Arango-only patterns.

suggestions.title: Make GraphIndex backend selection explicit and mutually exclusive
suggestions.rationale: `GraphIndexLoader._make_persistence()` currently selects SQLite whenever `_sqlite_dir` is set and otherwise selects ArangoDB when persistence is enabled; the factory documents only SQLite/Postgres. Adding a `backend='helixdb'` branch without an explicit precedence rule can silently choose the existing backend when callers pass legacy arguments.

suggestions.title: Specify atomic commit ordering, edge identity, and revert conflict semantics
suggestions.rationale: SQLite guarantees edge uniqueness with a primary key `(source_id, target_id, kind)` and detects later revert conflicts using commit `rowid`. Helix is a multigraph, and the proposal's find-then-add edge operation can race across HTTP clients. The design needs a stable edge key, an atomically allocated per-tenant commit sequence, and a precise compare-before-revert rule including incident edges removed with nodes.

suggestions.title: Use generation-based PageIndex projection or a durable outbox
suggestions.rationale: PageIndex writes the JSON tree and markdown sidecars separately, and `splice_subtree()` renumbers node IDs tree-wide before `_save_node_markdown()` and `_persist()`. An incremental Helix projection keyed only by `node_id` can retain stale nodes or attach bodies to the wrong node after a splice. Project complete tree generations or record durable projection events and reconcile them before serving Helix search.

suggestions.title: Put BookStore's async Helix adapter below the async Library boundary
suggestions.rationale: `CatalogStore` is deliberately synchronous and opens short-lived `sqlite3` connections, while `Library.search()` is async and calls synchronous catalog search through `_catalogs`. Directly delegating `CatalogStore.search()` to `helixdb.AsyncClient` would require unsafe loop bridging and lifecycle management. Use an async projection/search adapter owned by `Library`, or an explicitly isolated worker, and define behavior when canonical SQLite commits but projection writes fail.

suggestions.title: Add generic backend connection settings and fix namespace dispatch
suggestions.rationale: The project and environment-overlay models currently contain only `arango_*` connection fields. Federation also auto-converts a `database` entry to ArangoDB and passes `arango_params` into registered extra factories. Helix needs a backend-neutral connection model or explicit per-backend adapters so database names, URL/API-key prefixes, mode, read-only state, and server versus embedded source are resolved without Arango-specific arguments.

suggestions.title: Build a backend contract matrix rather than only live-server smoke tests
suggestions.rationale: Existing tests separately exercise concurrent CAS behavior, GraphIndex publish/revert/conflict behavior, SQLite persistence, and backend registration. Helix tests should run the same behavioral contract against embedded InMemory and the exact server image, covering read-only writes, CAS races, source-slice replacement, attrs/symbols/meta/lint methods, tenant isolation, close/reopen, and failure during index bootstrap.

suggestions.title: Add a compatibility gate for the SDK, embedded wheel, and pinned image
suggestions.rationale: The repository currently has no Helix dependency or per-file exemption, while the proposed client, embedded runtime, and server are independently versioned. Before implementing seven stores, CI should verify that `helix-db==0.3.4` speaks to the pinned image, that async-only usage is enforced, and that the native wheel imports on every supported architecture; otherwise failures will appear as backend logic defects.

suggestions.title: Define migration and rollback before exposing a backend switch
suggestions.rationale: The existing wiki export is an OKF pages/edges projection, not a full-fidelity migration of attrs, symbols, meta, embeddings, and source state. Ledger state is additionally represented by an append-only event log, and GraphIndex commits have separate audit/pre-image records. Merely changing configuration can open an empty Helix plane or lose rollback data; add explicit migration/rebuild commands with counts, checkpoints, and verification, or document a required canonical-source rebuild.

suggestions.title: Preserve existing search filtering and score semantics explicitly
suggestions.rationale: The SQLite wiki search excludes `archive` pages by default and returns cosine scores in `[-1,1]`; Postgres explicitly converts cosine distance to `1 - distance`. The Helix mapping mentions concatenated text and `$distance` but does not specify archive filtering, category behavior, score conversion, zero-vector handling, or dimension mismatch behavior. These must be contract-tested before ranking changes are considered drop-in.
